bullets.title: Bessent/Treasury Signals Roil Rates; BofA Cash at 3.5% Contrarian Sell
bullets.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent explicitly flagged that yields don't reflect fundamentals and signaled buybacks could exceed the announced $4B; the 30-year yield hit 5.31% (highest since 2007) before reversing 10bps. Separately, BofA's fund manager survey shows cash at 3.5%—the 6th-lowest since 1998—alongside 49% of respondents expecting stagflation, and an 'AI bubble' cited as the top tail risk by 32%. Goldman and JPMorgan each issued caution on autumn correction risk.

bullets.title: NVDA: Vera Rubin Ramps, Backs $105B OpenAI Ohio Data Center, Funds SB Energy
bullets.body: Microsoft confirmed receipt of first production Vera Rubin racks; NVIDIA separately announced it will provide credit support for 4.25 IT-GW at OpenAI's PORTS-Pike Technology Campus in Ohio, with a $1.5B investment in SB Energy. UBS estimates NVDA could generate $1B/day in FCF; BofA sum-of-parts sees 34–50% undervaluation. Bearish: NVDA led all stocks in bearish options flow on 8/19, and both NVDA and ORCL CDS hit all-time wides after Broadcom's $100B off-balance-sheet SPV.

bullets.title: Marvell Grants Google $12.2B Share Warrant in Custom Silicon Deal; MRVL Surges
bullets.body: Marvell issued Google a warrant to purchase up to 58.97M shares (~7% of company) through fiscal 2033 in exchange for a multi-billion custom silicon partnership covering AI inference accelerators, storage, and NICs for TPUs. MRVL popped ~6–13% on the news; analyst firm Oppenheimer raised PT to $300 from $250 and TD Cowen raised to $225. The deal is viewed as materially negative for AVGO, which had been Google's incumbent.

bullets.title: AAPL: Cuts 200+ Jobs in Siri/Vision Pro Teams; Weighs Chinese CXMT Memory
bullets.body: Apple is eliminating most of its Vision Pro gaming team and cutting Siri-related headcount (200+ positions). Separately, field-level sources and UBS suggest Apple is evaluating CXMT (Chinese DRAM) for China-market iPhones post a Trump-Xi September meeting, with memory reportedly already completing testing. An analyst also noted Apple pays ~$17B/year in Irish taxes and Walmart now supports Apple Pay.

bullets.title: META Faces $1.4T Antitrust Trial; Stock -15–20% YTD, Now at 10x OCF
bullets.body: Four state AGs opened trial in Oakland alleging META deliberately designed Facebook and Instagram to addict youth; California AG is seeking penalties, restitution, and market distortion remedies over six to seven weeks. Stock is down ~16–20% YTD, the worst among Mag 7/Mag 8. One analyst notes META trading at 10x this year's operating cash flow, comparable to its 2022 lows. META has also quietly become one of Microsoft's largest AI customers.

bullets.title: TSLA: Nevada AV Permit, Cybercab Austin Launch, JPMorgan Factory Tour
bullets.body: Tesla cleared for 5,000 autonomous vehicles in Nevada for paid robotaxi service. The Information reports Tesla told staff it is gearing up for a public Cybercab launch in Austin this month (first steering-wheel-free vehicle). JPMorgan visited the Fremont factory as humanoid production nears. Separately, Tesla recalled 2.74M China-made Model 3/Y vehicles over door software, and suspended Solar Roof tiles after determining the product is not economically viable. $56–58M in bullish options flow was flagged intraday on 8/20.

bullets.title: MU: $10B Micron Research Labs; S&P Upgrades to BBB+; CEO Visits Boise
bullets.body: Micron announced a $10B Micron Research Labs initiative spanning decades to advance memory and compute; S&P upgraded MU's credit rating to BBB+ with a positive outlook. Jim Cramer toured the Boise facility and called for a double. Analyst notes 40TB Micron/Primemask external memory system being installed at a U.S. national research lab. Semiconductor sector fell 5% on 8/18, SOXX down 7.7% over two days, then partially recovered.

bullets.title: SNDK Up 80% From Leopold Lows; AAOI Dilution Concerns; LITE/COHR Recovery
bullets.body: SanDisk surged as much as 80% from the Leopold Aschenbrenner hedge fund blow-up lows, emerging as the S&P 500's top YTD performer at +653%. AAOI is facing pushback over repeated $500–600M ATM equity offerings; Rosenblatt maintained Buy with $750 PT but acknowledged dilution will be 'less important' over time. LITE and COHR both recovered 39–41% in under three weeks per one analyst's disclosed portfolio; multiple accounts flagged extreme demand imbalance in lasers and TIA.

bullets.title: US-Canada Trade: 50% Tariffs Imposed; Retaliatory Duties Effective Sep 8
bullets.body: US-Canada trade deal collapsed at the last minute after both governments accused each other of changing agreed terms. 50% Section 338 tariffs on Canadian goods went into effect Saturday; Canada announced dollar-for-dollar retaliation effective September 8 targeting steel, dairy, and other sectors. Canada suspended negotiations. Earlier in the week Trump had briefly paused tariffs for 3 days, raising hopes, but talks broke down. Canada's PM Carney said the country is now 'at war' with the US on trade.

bullets.title: AVGO: $100B Off-Balance-Sheet SPV; CDS at Record Wide
bullets.body: Broadcom announced a $60–100B off-balance-sheet SPV deal for AI chip financing, reportedly to supply Anthropic with custom ASICs. AVGO CDS hit a record 122 at close and NVDA CDS also hit all-time wides. The structure involves Broadcom-backed lenders, potentially drawing from insurance pools. Analysts noted this is materially positive for Broadcom's custom ASIC pipeline but raises balance-sheet and credit risk questions.

bullets.title: AI Capex/Debt Issuance Creates Global Bond Pressure; 30Y Hits 5.31%
bullets.body: The US 30-year Treasury yield reached 5.31% (highest since June 2007), with analysts attributing it partly to record AI-related corporate debt issuance crowding out government bonds. Nine major tech firms reportedly have ~$3T in off-balance-sheet AI commitments vs. $600B in reported capex. Goldman and Citadel warned that Fed policy is keeping long-end yields elevated while Morgan Stanley raised its Amazon price target to $500 on AWS/AI growth.

bullets.title: INTC: Foundry Inflection; CEO Buys $10M; Razor Lake to Use TSMC 2nm
bullets.body: Intel Foundry reported Q1 FY27 operating loss narrowed $348M QoQ, external revenue up 68% to $293M. CEO Lip-Bu Tan purchased $10M in INTC stock, reportedly the largest insider buy in company history. Razor Lake desktop CPUs are rumored to use TSMC's N2X process. AMD and NVIDIA each only shared benchmarks; Intel has not yet disclosed results in new efficiency metrics. Rack-scale compute expected to grow from <10% to 35–40% of accelerator install base over the coming years.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Pixel Supply Chain Exits China by 2027; Waymo Hits 1.4M Rides/Month
bullets.body: Google has reportedly told suppliers it plans to have all Pixel smartphones, watches, and earbuds produced outside China by 2027, shifting to Vietnam and India. Waymo now executes over 1.4M monthly rides in California, a 10x increase in two years, and disclosed its custom 5nm ASIC chip. Berkshire Hathaway disclosed GOOGL as its 3rd-largest holding.

bullets.title: Amazon Expands Louisiana Data Center Investment to $18B; Prime Air Drone Deliveries
bullets.body: Amazon increased its Louisiana data center commitment from $12B to $18B with a third campus planned. Amazon also announced drone delivery expansion to suburban Chicago and Atlanta and partnered with Zipline targeting 1M daily drone deliveries by 2029. Microsoft CFO disclosed that $25B of 2026 CapEx is a surcharge for higher memory and storage component costs.

bullets.title: UBER: €825M GDPR Fine from Dutch Authorities; Autonomous Rides in Zagreb
bullets.body: Dutch authorities fined Uber €825M ($963M)—the second-largest GDPR penalty on record—for using automated systems to improperly suspend driver accounts. Separately, Uber launched autonomous rides in Zagreb (first European city) via Verne and Pony AI, and UBER sold 72M shares of Aurora Innovation at $6.55. Manhattan service quality complaints noted: 50% driver no-show rate flagged.

bullets.title: EQIX: Singapore Awards 200MW Capacity; Trump Files EQIX Purchase
bullets.body: Singapore provisionally awarded 200MW in its low-carbon data center park on Jurong Island, with Equinix among four recipients. Separately, Trump reportedly filed a purchase of up to $1,000,000 in Equinix stock, citing interest in data center investments as a hypothetical small-town mayor.

bullets.title: SPOT: Spotify Adds $1.5B to Buyback; Volumes Surge
bullets.body: Spotify announced an additional $1.5B share repurchase, adding to existing buyback. Separately, a user noted Spotify volume surging 273% in Korea as retail re-entered crypto markets, though the 'spot volumes' tweet may conflate the ticker with commodity spot prices.

bullets.title: DIS: ABC Sues FCC; FCC Scrutiny of Disney Broadcast Licenses
bullets.body: Disney and ABC filed a lawsuit seeking to halt the FCC's early license renewal proceeding. Separately, a LightShed analyst flagged DIS with an FCC scrutiny indicator. First Lady Melania Trump announced a partnership with IndyCar and FOX Corporation for a youth initiative, briefly pushing FOXA into news.

bullets.title: NBIS/CRWV: Nebius Plans $4.5B Convertible; CoreWeave Backlog at $104B
bullets.body: Nebius announced a $4.5B convertible senior notes offering to fund AI data center expansion—largest single debt raise in the company's history. CoreWeave's revenue backlog reached $104B, nearly 2x its market cap. Goldman is gauging demand for a $1.15B junk bond to fund a CoreWeave-leased Virginia data center. A $2M far-OTM call order was flagged on NBIS at the 440 strike.

bullets.title: IREN: 800MW Australia Site; Regulatory Headwinds; Bipartisan Data Center Opposition
bullets.body: Social media flagged IREN may have secured a massive hidden advantage via an 800MW Australian site. Pennsylvania Governor Shapiro signed an executive order restricting data center development; Texas Governor Abbott halted up to 1,800 data center projects; Ohio and New York also imposing restrictions. One commenter called bipartisan data center opposition 'the one thing the left and the right agree on.' Ticker IREN also appeared in Iran-sanctions context (Iran ticker mismatch).
